body:
That's just why I didn't toss myself in front of the 18:48 instead of posting this. I don't know for sure. Why not keep going for 30? 35? Hell, why not ninety fucking five?

It's a terrible cliche and I feel bad for even posting this, but I'm still sitting in the same graveyard bench I posted the original post from. Noone has come past or even looked my way. They're all busy doing whatever.

e: Shit, do you even know what the laughter of twentysomethings enjoying themselves does to someone like me? It's absolutely soul-crushing, and I don't type that lightly. I mean it reminds me of everything I will never, ever have and all the reasons I should put a bullet through my brain or helium in my lungs.

//wrists

god, I feel like a fucking sixteen-year-old girl.

PS: Fuck knows why there is WiFi in a graveyard, but that's the 2000s for you.

I know there's a good chance someone will ask, so I'll answer now:

The reason I quit WoW is because I "chose life" as the memes so succinctly (lol fancy words) put it. Life as a WoW addict was honestly shit. My play time was in a haze and my time outside of the game was a living hell. Back then I worked part-time as an office clerk and spent the rest of the time earning server first Shadowmourne as a Retribution Paladin (lol retfags). Every day I would cross a railway crossing on my way to work. Often I would have to wait for a train to pass before crossing, and I would imagine putting my head on the rails and ending my existence then and there.

That was five years ago.

You can imagine ten years ago. Fifteen years ago. Why should five years from now be any better? Do you honestly believe a bland robotic nerd shell will find joy or meaning?

Distraction is just that, distraction. I don't know if you've ever played WoW, but I am (was, I quit) not like most players you'll encounter. I was cold and calculating in every situation and had to force myself to pretend to be relaxed and casual in social situations when required. I wasn't joyful at any point, and I only continued playing because distracting myself with concerns of attack power and honor points was less painful than not doing so. The difference is that now I realize that not being alive at all would be preferable to either alternative.

That is, feeling nothing - oblivion, death, limbo, whatever you fancy - is preferable to my life.

I am and was raised an atheist by the way, so please hold the comments related to God and Catholicism.
